CGM 74 mg/dL at 14:50, 55 at 15:20, 46 at 15:38. Watch HR rose from 84 to 118 bpm between 15:30 and 15:40. Day-centre checklist 15:40: pale, sweaty, slurring, wants to sit down. Glucometer 44 mg/dL at 15:44. Juice given 15:46; CGM 61 mg/dL at 16:10.
cases.rationale: The meter confirms 44 mg/dL with pallor, sweating, slurred speech and a heart rate that rose about 34 bpm, so the danger-level low is symptomatic and confirmed on a reliable reading. The four checks: the reading is reliable and confirmed, no explanation applies because the lunch and insulin were recorded, the patient has no hospice plan, and the baseline is irrelevant to a danger value, so the tier is ABSOLUTE. The lunch was small against a full lispro dose, which is a pattern clinicians need to see now. Naive-model trap: a shallow model sees a patient who recovered to 61 mg/dL after juice and routes nurse_task, when a symptomatic confirmed low on insulin needs a page now.
cases.decisive_feature: A meter-confirmed 44 mg/dL with pallor, sweating and slurred speech after a full lispro dose and half a lunch at the day centre, so the low is symptomatic and needs a page now.
